Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (C/C077/C077n1710.xml). Recorded Sayings of Ancient Venerable Masters. Baiyun Shouduan owns the retained address: the founder asked who would vouch for the true line — one saw the Akshobha realm and never saw again: skin; one held no single thing against his feeling: flesh; the Second Founder bowed three times and stood in place at his station: marrow. Had I seen the three of them answer so, a good thirty sticks each — and Baiyun today is due twenty-nine himself, leaving one for all of you; whoever feels the sting neither fails the old sages nor misses Baiyun; failing that — you chew your gruel in the hall, but most of you swallow it down in one muddy lump.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB159.xml). Essential Sayings of Chan Master Tianzhen Dufengshan. Dufeng Shan owns the retained essay: Great Master Huike — no book he could not explain, no scripture he had not mastered — yet before the First Founder he could not frame one word, and only then sought mind-calming; from that he dropped everything, mind like a wall; snow-standing and arm-cutting still won no nod; then one sudden breakthrough — three bows, standing in place at his station, and at last the word: you have my marrow. Was that a casual feat? Lately students, coarse of mind, take the finger for the moon, misread it themselves, and stamp it on later generations — one blind man leading a crowd of blind men.

Occurrences.Kwic: 示韓叔夜居士初祖達磨西來不為別事，只求一個不自欺不被人欺底人而已矣！二祖神光初見達磨，更不求西來所傳底意旨，但曰：「弟子此心不安，請師為我安心。」達磨亦不教彼參究我西來所傳底意旨，但曰：「將心來為汝安！」光曰：「覓心了不可得？」磨曰：「為汝安心竟。」光於言下大悟。異日，磨復問諸門人各言所得，獨神光作禮三拜依位而立，磨曰：「汝得吾髓。」只此便是達磨與神光不自欺，亦不被人欺也。使達磨不深見神光真見不自欺處，雖與曰：「為汝安心竟。」神光安能直下證悟？使今人亦曰：「我亦覓心了不可得。」心既不可得，則一切法亦不可得；真如佛性菩提涅槃，乃至一千七百機綠公案皆不可得。且道此人還真自欺否？若真不自欺，則不被人欺，亦終不肯欺天下古

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B27/B27n0152.xml). Recorded Sayings of National Master Puji Yulin. Yulin Tongxiu owns the retained small-meeting: the season turns to the new year, so this mountain monk sets out the teeth and claws of the founding teachers to rouse fresh spirit in you all — of old Wuzu Fayan raised how the founder bade his disciples each state what he had attained: not wed to words, not leaving them: skin; like Qingxi seeing the Akshobha realm, one look and never a second: flesh; the four elements empty from the start, not one thing to set against feeling: bone; last, Great Master Huike came out, bowed three times, stood in place at his station: marrow. Wuzu said: had I seen the four of them answer so, thirty sticks each — and this Baiyun of today is due twenty-nine, one stick left over for you; whoever feels the sting wrongs neither the old sages nor Baiyun; failing that, you chew your gruel in the hall but gulp it down whole — then he rapped his staff and called out: assembly! the king of the teaching has a true ear of his own.

Senses.Explanation: Bow three times, then stand in place at your station: the answer that won the marrow — raised at hall addresses, letters, record openers, and live challenges. Xutang Zhiyu, in the hall: you will not honestly walk your own field; you only want to till the official's land under a borrowed name — do you know: the Second Founder faced Bodhidharma, bowed three times, and stood in place at his station? Baiyun Shouduan, on the raised case: who will vouch for the true line? — one saw the Akshobha realm and never saw again: skin; one held nothing against his feeling: flesh; the Second Founder bowed three times and stood in place at his station: marrow — had I seen the three of them answer so, thirty sticks each; Baiyun today is due twenty-nine himself, one stick left for all of you; whoever feels the sting neither fails the old sages nor misses Baiyun — failing that, you chew your gruel in the hall but most of you swallow it down in one muddy lump. Dufeng Shan, in the essay: Great Master Huike, no book unexplained, no scripture unmastered, could not frame one word before the First Founder and only then sought mind-calming; everything dropped, mind like a wall; snow-standing and arm-cutting won no nod; then one sudden breakthrough — three bows, standing in place, you have my marrow: was that a casual feat? — while lately students take the finger for the moon, stamp their misreading on later generations, one blind man leading a crowd of blind. Juelang Daosheng, writing to the layman: on a later day the founder asked each disciple to state what he had attained; Shen'guang alone bowed three times and stood in place at his station — you have my marrow — this very thing is the two of them neither fooling themselves nor being fooled. Foyuan Chegang, opening the record: the first truth was already beheld when the World-Honored raised the flower and his first disciple smiled; at the end the arm-cutting fellow merely bowed three times and stood in place at his station — already beheld — so what more is there to behold? step out and meet me. Yushan Shangsi, in the live exchange: a monk stepped out, finished his bow, and at once stood in place — of old the Second Founder stood in place, and Bodhidharma called it winning the marrow: what have you won today? do not bewilder people, please — the hair has not even reached you yet. Yulin Tongxiu, at the New Year small-meeting: the founders' teeth and claws, to rouse fresh spirit — Wuzu Fayan raised the founder's each-state-what-you-attained: skin, flesh, bone; last, Great Master Huike came out, bowed three times, stood in place: marrow — thirty sticks each had he seen them, this Baiyun of today due twenty-nine, one stick left for you; whoever feels the sting wrongs neither the old sages nor Baiyun; failing that, the gruel gulped down whole — and he rapped his staff: assembly! the king of the teaching has a true ear of his own.
